Issue 511 unit 6 (items 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6) is built in `crates/ingest/src/partyname.rs`, `crates/ingest/src/project.rs` and `crates/app/src/supervisor.rs`. The final focused run passed: EXIT=0, 163 passed, 0 failed (`u6-build/logs/final-focused.log`). Nothing is committed and ops/check.sh was not run. Code first, then tests, then a mutation pass at the end: each of 10 single-point mutations made at least one new test fail (`u6-build/logs/mutations-summary.txt`).

**Item 1 — a name right after the reference, with no separator** (partyname.rs:1127, `opens_with_a_name` at :1149)
- When a pointer stem's section reference is followed directly by a name, the party is kept as AwardSummary. The name must be the first word after the references, the section titles and any position word. It must be capitalised, have at least two letters, and not be a closed-list word.
- Kept: 'Please see section VI.4.3 Translink', 'See section VI.4.3 Translink', 'See Section VI.3 Kier Construction', 'Siehe oben VI.4.1 Vergabekammer Südbayern'. 'S. VI.4.1) Weimar Deutschland' stays a name.
- Still Placeholder: 'See Section VI.3 Additional information', 'please see Section VI.3.2', '… for list of awarded Suppliers', '… of the Project Information Memorandum', 'See section VI.2 Avis'.
- Test: `a_name_right_after_a_pointers_reference_is_kept` (:4192). I updated the premises in the existing tests that expected Translink and Kier to be Placeholder. ORG-16 (project.rs:14876) now pins the bare-seed rule those cases used to pin.

**Item 2 — the readers' junk**
- Closed lists extended:
  - pointer words (:1340): as shown in, as defined in, as set out, as noted in, se referer, se reporter;
  - nouns (:1674): body, those, named, link(s), detailed, instructions, answer, stelle, bezeichnete, kontaktdaten, gestelde, citees, url;
  - notice words: contract award notice, appel à candidatures, avviso di gara, corresponding, original, the typo presenta;
  - joiner: het;
  - positions: remain(s) the same;
  - typo locators: abschnittt, abschnit, rubirque;
  - title typo: kontakstelle.
- Every listed 'As …' form now classifies Placeholder. So do 'See links detailed in II.1.5', the 'Se référer à l'article VI.3 …', 'See VI.4.1) Review body field …' and 'Siehe die unter Ziffer VI.4.1) genannte Stelle.' sentences, plus their kin.
- The residual's 'same as (in point) VI.x', 'please refer to VI.x', 'as in (point) VI.x' and 'voir point VI.x' forms were already Placeholder; they are pinned in the test.
- The long UK sentences went in as 4 exact whole values (:299). The Hertfordshire variants that carry the council's name stay names.
- Test: `the_as_family_and_the_readers_junk_are_section_reference_pointers` (:4244).

**Item 3 — mixed folds.** The residual plan shows the kept spellings: 'Wie VI.4 1)', 'Voir section VI.4 2', 'siehe I.1 oder VI 4.1' and 'Siehe VI.4. 1)'. A reference now accepts a space in place of the second dot, a space after a dot, or the numeral spaced off its number (`has_form_reference` :1791, `spaced_last` :1845). Only the last group can stand off, it must be one or two digits, and no dotted group may follow it, so dates and years stay out. Test: `a_spaced_section_reference_is_one_reference` (:4334).

**Item 4 — the dry plan's legal_form list** now leaves out section-reference pointers (`plan_legal_form` :959; supervisor.rs:5528). Tests: `the_plans_legal_form_list_leaves_out_section_reference_pointers` (:4368) and the supervisor test `the_placeholder_plans_legal_form_list_leaves_out_section_reference_pointers` (supervisor.rs:17293). On the plans, 227 of residual 2310's 268 entries leave the list, and 536 of dry 2283's 665.

**Item 6 — 19530163 ORG-10 and the TED template signal**
- Only two of the 24 copies kept the party: PT 'Consultar …' and SL 'Glejte …'. Their openers were in no list, so they were neither pointers nor translations to the echo.
- I added those two openers, the EL, PT, SV and CS titles, and the locators punkti, szakaszt (postposed) and 't taqsima'. All 24 copies now classify Placeholder on their own.
- New `template_echoes` (project.rs:4698), called first in `translation_echoes`. The seed is an English-labelled bare placeholder with a section number; unit 5's section-reference pointers count as seeds here. When at least 10 distinct labels carry that number in short copies with no legal form, every unclassified copy that is pointer-led or framed is swept, whatever its opener. Framed means a locator just before the reference or a title just after it (`template_shaped` :903, `reference_framed` :919).
- The walk's net arm `echo_shaped` (:869) now uses `template_shaped`, so the net still holds every name the fold can sweep.
- Tests:
  - `teds_19530163_pointer_drops_in_every_template_wording`: the 24 verbatim copies; the party drops whichever copy heads it.
  - `the_ted_template_signal_sweeps_copies_whatever_their_opener`: copies with unknown openers; 9 languages are kept, 10 drop.
  - `the_ted_template_signal_keeps_a_named_party`: a company whose one copy has a legal form, a bilingual body, no English seed, a non-bare seed, unlabelled copies, another section number.
  - `teds_earlier_template_wordings_are_pointers_and_template_copies` (:4403).
- The superset test now also asserts that every literal the echo or the template could sweep is a net hit (:4498).

**Simulation.** New `issue_511_unit_6_simulation` (:4641) runs a shared helper `simulate_plan` (:4698); the unit 5 harness now calls the same helper. Output is in `u6-build/simulation.md` and `u6-build/simulation.json`.

| name → placeholder | 65 folds / 86 orgs / 429 mentions / 0 buyer rows | 61 folds / 78 orgs / 412 mentions / 0 buyer rows |
| other transitions | none | 1 fold placeholder → award_summary (Translink) |
| net orgs / buyer rows | 1,648 / 102 (unchanged) | 22,579 / 115 (unit 5: 22,453 / 114) |
| added by the framed shape | 0 | 126 orgs / 1 buyer row |

**Doubts**
- **Template signal reading.** I implemented "whatever their opener" with a structural guard, because a literal "any short copy carrying the number" needs unit 4's wide net arm, about 1,160 more buyer rows on dry 2283. The guard:
  - the reference sits within the first 4 words;
  - after the first word, the opener words are lowercase or closed-list words, never a pointer word;
  - there is no separator or full stop before the reference;
  - the copy is framed (locator before or title after).

  Under this guard, a hypothetical 10-plus-language party whose English copy is a bare pointer while its other copies read like 'Acme, punkt VI.3' would drop. The keep test documents this. With two capitalised words ('Acme Bau, punkt VI.3') the copy is not swept.
- **Not simulated.** The template sweep is decided per party across a notice's copies. The plans hold only head names, so the simulation shows the net cost but not how many parties drop. Whether the residual's 'same as / please refer to / as in' parties have 10 or more labelled copies with an English one was not read (needs prod). If their siblings are fewer, they stay kept.
- **The unit-4 canary is still mandatory** before the unit 6 wet: refold 12516947 and 19530163 and assert ORG-2 and ORG-10 are gone.
- **Left as names, not in this item's lists:** 'As above (Please see IV.4.1)', 'Please refer to VI.4.3) as above', 'As stated at V.1 3.1 above', 'As per Regulation 50(6)(a) …', 'Name Withheld for security reasons' (10 mentions), 'Details of supplier withheld for reasons of security', 'Supplier name withheld for the protection of vulnerable individuals', and 'Due to the sensitive nature of this Contract the suppliers name is being withheld'. 'The High Court' after a reference with no separator still stays Placeholder, as before.
- **Disk.** I briefly started one mutation run with `-p ingest` alone, which CLAUDE.md warns builds a second artifact family. I stopped it within seconds and deleted exactly the 84 artifacts it created (about 22 MiB, all newer than my last gate-flag build). 8.0 GB free at the end, the same as at the start.

All logs and outputs are under `/home/user/tender-db/.scratch/tender-db/511-placeholders/u6-build/`.

findings.title: The echo and template sweeps take a copy that names a body right after its reference, and unit 6's new openers make more copies sweepable
findings.scenario: Item 1 treats a name right after a pointer's reference as a body, but only when the opener is a placeholder stem: 'Siehe oben VI.4.1 Vergabekammer Südbayern' is AwardSummary. The two sweeps never ask that question. This unit adds `consultar` and `glejte`, the short `se referer`/`se reporter`, and `as shown in`/`as defined in`/`as set out`/`as noted in` to SECTION_POINTERS (partyname.rs:1342-1466). That makes `pointer_led`, and so unit 5's TWO-language `translation_echoes`, cover copies that were names on HEAD. Example: a bilingual review-body party with EN 'See section VI.4.1' and SL 'Glejte oddelek VI.4.1 Državna revizijska komisija'. My probe (a temporary integration test calling only the crate's public functions, run with the gate's flags; since deleted) showed: EN copy is Placeholder, echo_seed=true, token vi.4.1; SL copy has not_a_name=None and translation_shaped=true with the same token. The echo marks the SL copy Placeholder, every name is now Placeholder, and the real body is dropped. On HEAD `glejte` was not a pointer, so the copy was not swept and the party was kept. The same happens with FR 'Se référer au point VI.4.1 Conseil d'État' and PT 'Consultar o ponto VI.4.1 Tribunal Administrativo de Círculo de Lisboa' (both None and translation_shaped now). It also happens with EN copies such as 'As set out at VI.4.1 Office of Government Procurement' beside a non-English stem seed like 'Siehe oben VI.4.1' (echo_seed=true). In a party with 10 or more languages, `template_echoes` (line 4726) sweeps all of these too, since they are template_shaped. Unit 5's review rated the same shape should-fix (FI 'Katso kohta VI.4.1' sweeping SV 'Se punkt VI.4.1 Marknadsdomstolen'). Among the 5,356 head spellings in the u4/u45 plans, every new-opener spelling is a bare pointer. Translated copies are not head names, though, so the plans cannot show this case.
findings.fix: In both `translation_echoes` and `template_echoes`, do not sweep a copy whose text after its last form-section reference opens with a name. Blank the form titles, skip the positions, then reuse `opens_with_a_name` (for example through a new pub helper `partyname::names_after_reference(raw)`). This cannot touch any 19530163 or 12516947 copy: each is a section-reference pointer by itself, so its tail is all closed-list words, and `opens_with_a_name` refuses those. Add keep cases to the tests: EN 'See section VI.4.1' paired with each of 'Glejte oddelek VI.4.1 Državna revizijska komisija' and 'Se référer au point VI.4.1 Conseil d'État', and a 24-copy party where one copy names a body after its reference. A name BEFORE the locator ('Marknadsdomstolen punkt VI.4.1', 'Translink, section VI.4.3', both template_shaped) remains the trade-off the build report already lists as a doubt.

findings.title: Item 1's opens_with_a_name keeps the lexicon's own non-name words and capitalised German nouns, and brings back names unit 3 already dropped
findings.scenario:
Before unit 6, a pointer stem followed by a reference and no separator was always Placeholder. Now any capitalised first word of 2+ letters that is not a closed-list word turns it into AwardSummary, which the fold never drops. The walk's requeues() also exempts an AwardSummary head, so such an org is never revisited. Verified with a probe built with the gate flags (since deleted):
- The lexicon's own non-name words: 'See section VI.3 Not applicable', '… TBC', '… Various', '… Withheld', '… Confidential', '… Unknown', '… Nil'.
- Form and generic labels: 'See section I.1 Name and addresses', 'See Section V.2.3 Name and address of the contractor', 'Please see section VI.4.1 Mediation body', 'See section VI.4.3 Contact details', 'See section VI.3 Contracts Finder', '… Suppliers', 'See Section VI.3 Lots 1-5', '… Annex', 'See section VI.4.3 Service from which information about the lodging of appeals may be obtained'.
- German nouns, which are always capitalised: 'siehe oben VI.4.1 Nachprüfungsstelle', 'siehe oben Ziffer VI.4.1 Zuständige Stelle', 'siehe oben I.1 Adresse', '… Ansprechpartner', '… Name', 'siehe oben II.1.4 Kurze Beschreibung', 'siehe oben VI.3 Weitere Angaben'.
- A Roman numeral left over when strip_references cannot split a glued token: 'siehe oben Ziff. VI.4.1Ort' reads 'VI' as the name.

Three real names in u3/plan-2265.json and plan-2266.json were Placeholder, were dropped by unit 3's wet, and are now AwardSummary: 'Siehe oben Abschnitt II.1.4). Es handelt sich um eine freiwillige EU-Bekanntmachung …' (6 mentions), 'See Section VI.3 Additonal Information, sub-section 2.' and 'siehe oben Ziff. VI.4.1Ort'. Any refold of their notices re-mints them as kept orgs. The u6 simulation cannot see this: it only re-reads orgs that still exist, these were swept, and the 2265/2266 non_exact lists stop at 700 folds. No test pins a capitalised generic word as a near miss.
findings.fix: Refuse a tail the lexicon classes by itself (not_a_name of the tail is Some(Placeholder or Blank)). Skip a bare ROMAN word the same way roman_with_digits is skipped. Add the missing form labels (name and address(es), mediation body, contact point, the VI.4.3 service title, DE Nachprüfungsstelle and Zuständige Stelle) to FORM_SECTION_TITLES or the noun list. Add near-miss assertions for the strings above. Then re-run simulate_plan on u3/plan-2265.json and plan-2266.json to count which previously dropped names would come back.

findings.title: A title right after the reference frames the copy even when a body is named after the title
findings.scenario: template_shaped('VI.4.1) Review body: High Court of Justice') and template_shaped('VI.4.1) Instance chargée des procédures de recours: Tribunal administratif de Paris') are both true, while not_a_name returns None for both (they are names). Take a party in a 10+-language notice whose English seed is the bare label 'VI.4.1) Review body' (template_seed true) and whose FR copy names the court after the colon. findings.fix: In reference_framed, treat the title frame like the grammar's after-separator rule: after the title, allow only titles, positions, joiners or the end. Add the two strings as near misses.

fix:
I fixed all seven findings. F2, F4 and F7 are the same Translink finding, and that one has no code fix: it goes in the runbook, which I added to issue 511. The final focused run passed (`EXIT=0`: 276 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored), and the simulation re-ran with `EXIT=0`. Nothing is committed, `ops/check.sh` was not run, and I made no prod reads.

| Finding | Verdict | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| F1: the sweeps take a copy that names a body | Real (probe confirmed) | Fixed, with one deliberate change to the proposed fix (below) |
| F3: item 1 keeps non-names and labels | Real (all listed strings were AwardSummary) | Fixed |
| F5: class guard untested | Real | Test added |
| F6: `reference_framed` guards untested | Real (all six strings were false today) | Six strings added, one per guard |
| F2 / F4 / F7: Translink not restored | Real | Runbook step added to issue 511 |

**F1.** There are two new pub helpers in `partyname.rs`, `names_after_reference` and `titled_after_reference`. Both read the text after a copy's last form section reference. `translation_echoes` and `template_echoes` now leave a copy alone when that text opens with a name, unless the seed itself carries a section title after its reference.
- **Why not the fix as proposed:** applied unconditionally, it breaks unit 4's pinned behaviour. `Se punkt VI.2) Nye oplysninger` is a title the lists miss, and it reads exactly like a body name. Only the seed tells them apart: beside a bare seed (`See section VI.4.1`) the tail can only be a body, while beside a titled seed it is the translated title.
